result.method: pointwise pixel-value sampled on a grid over the shared extent (an estimate, not every pixel); windows where either map is no-data are dropped before any statistic; no ground truth, so this is model-vs-model agreement (no ground truth), not accuracy.
result.warning: the results measure different properties (['sample_karst_score', 'sample_number']), so their values are different quantities: only the correlation (whether they rise and fall together) is meaningful. Do not read the mean difference, RMSE or agreement fraction as a gap between them, and do not say one reads higher than the other.
result.sampling_note: the 6x6 grid has 36 cells; each of the 2 results was sampled once per cell, so 72 samples were requested; 25 compared, 11 dropped (no-data or failed in either map; n_nodata_dropped and n_failed_dropped count those cells)
result.nodata_rule: a sample is no-data, and never enters a statistic, when its band is missing or NaN, equals the model's nodata_value, lies outside the band's declared regression range, or carries no class on a classification band

content:
I compared the two completed 2025 runs on your PA Karst area ("Karst Features in Pennsylvania" project) by sampling both maps on a shared 6x6 grid (~10,091 km² of overlap).

**Key finding: they are different quantities, so no simple "gap"**

| | KarstBinary (`sample_karst_score`) | KarstNumber (`sample_number`) |
|---|---|---|
| Declared range | 0.0 – 1.0 | 0.2 – 1.2 |
| Mean over compared cells | 0.100 | 0.682 |
| No-data cells dropped | part of 11 of 36 total | |

Across the **25 comparable cells**:

- Correlation between the two: **-0.017** (essentially zero — they do not rise and fall together anywhere on the grid)
- Agreement (within ±0.1): **0%** — but caveat: since the ranges differ, the mean difference, RMSE (0.618) and max diff (0.719) compare different units and are *not* a meaningful measure of disagreement. Only the near-zero correlation is interpretable: the two maps mark up largely different places as karst.

**Which one is right?** That cannot be answered from these outputs alone — there are no ground-truth labels, so neither map can be graded for accuracy (model-vs-model agreement is not accuracy). To settle it you need reference labels, e.g.:

1. Label a confidence-based sample from one map, then estimate its error rate (honest accuracy test), or
2. Review a low-margin review set — the windows where each model is least confident — against field reports/USGS data.

Want me to set up a label-sample design for one of the two maps?
